help_fullreset_description: The `$fullreset` command allows the server owner to perform a full server reset. This command deletes all players, all coins, and all Elo from all users, as well as deleting all Player tuples from the server. This action is IRREVERSIBLE.
help_fullreset_usage:
```
$fullreset
```
• **No arguments**: The command does not require arguments. Just execute `$fullreset` and confirm with `y` or `n`.
help_fullreset_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Server owner only**: This command can only be used by the server owner.
• **Confirmation required**: The command will show a warning and ask for confirmation (y/n) with a 30-second timeout.
• **Irreversible action**: Once confirmed, it deletes:
  - All players from all users
  - All coins from all users
  - All Elo from all users
  - All Player tuples from the server
• **Statistics**: After execution, it shows statistics of what was deleted.
help_edittag_description: The `$edittag` (or `$etag`) command allows an administrator to change another user's tag. The tag is a short identifier displayed alongside the user's name. This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
help_edittag_usage:
```
$edittag @user new_tag
$etag @user new_tag
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user whose tag you want to change.
• **new_tag**: The new tag you want to assign (maximum 5 characters).
help_edittag_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Administrators only**: This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
• **Mention required**: You must mention the user whose tag you want to change.
• **Maximum length**: The tag must be 5 characters or less.
• **Immediate update**: The tag is updated immediately and the previous tag is shown if it existed.
help_trackpick_description: The `$trackpick` command allows you to assign a track to one of your preferred track types. You can have up to 2 tracks per type (slot A and slot B). Available types are: top, antitop, bottom, and balanced.
help_trackpick_usage:
```
$trackpick <type> "<track name>"
$trackpick <type> <abbreviation>
```
• **type**: Track type (top, antitop, bottom, balanced).
• **track name**: Track name in quotes. If it contains spaces, it must be in quotes. You can use the name in Spanish, English, or French.
• **abbreviation**: Track abbreviation without quotes (e.g., `MBC` for Mario Circuit).
help_trackpick_examples:
```
$trackpick top "Mirador Estelar"
$trackpick bottom "Mario Circuit"
$trackpick balanced "Rainbow Road"
$trackpick top MBC
```
help_trackpick_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Track types**: You can assign tracks to 4 different types: top (preferred top tracks), antitop (preferred antitop tracks), bottom (preferred bottom tracks), and balanced (preferred balanced tracks).
• **Two slots per type**: Each type has 2 slots (A and B), allowing you to have up to 2 tracks per type.
• **Name in quotes**: The track name must be in quotes if it contains spaces.
• **Multi-language search**: You can use the track name in Spanish, English, or French, or its abbreviation (use `$trackinfo` to see the abbreviations).
• **Abbreviations without quotes**: Abbreviations can be used without quotes (e.g., `$trackpick top MBC`).
• **Restrictions**: You cannot have the same track in both slots of the same type.
help_trackremove_description: The `$trackremove` command allows you to remove one or all tracks assigned to a specific type. You can remove all tracks of a type or specify a specific track.
help_trackremove_usage:
```
$trackremove <type>
$trackremove <type> "<track name>"
$trackremove <type> <abbreviation>
```
• **type**: Track type (top, antitop, bottom, balanced).
• **track name** (optional): Specific track name to remove in quotes. If it contains spaces, it must be in quotes.
• **abbreviation** (optional): Track abbreviation without quotes (e.g., `MBC`). If not specified, all tracks of that type are removed.
help_trackremove_examples:
```
$trackremove top "Mirador Estelar"
$trackremove bottom "Mario Circuit"
$trackremove balanced "Rainbow Road"
$trackremove top MBC
```
help_trackremove_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Remove all tracks**: If you only specify the type, all tracks of that type are removed (both slot A and B).
• **Remove specific track**: If you specify the type and the track name in quotes, only that specific track is removed.
• **Automatic reorganization**: If you remove a track from slot A and there is a track in slot B, the track from slot B will automatically move to slot A.
• **Multi-language search**: You can use the track name in Spanish, English, or French, or its abbreviation (use `$trackinfo` to see the abbreviations).
• **Abbreviations without quotes**: Abbreviations can be used without quotes (e.g., `$trackremove top MBC`).
• **Validation**: The command verifies that the track is assigned before removing it.
help_train_description: The `$train` command allows you to train one of your players to improve their attributes. The command is interactive and will show you a menu with different training options. Each training consumes one training session from your counter.
help_train_usage:
```
$train <player name>
$train "player name"
```
• **player name**: Name or alias of the player you want to train. You can use quotes if the name has spaces.
help_train_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Player required**: You must specify the name or alias of a player you have in your roster.
• **Interactive menu**: The command will show a menu with 8 training options (1-7 are specific trainings, 8 is to focus an attribute).
• **Focused training**: If you choose option 8, you can choose which attribute to focus, which will receive +33 points.
• **Random effects**: Trainings 1-7 have random effects on different attributes.
• **Stats limit**: A player's total stats cannot exceed 8000 points. If exceeded, they are automatically adjusted.
• **Once per reset**: Each player can only be trained once per reset.
• **Session consumption**: Each training consumes one training session from your counter.
help_accept_description: The `$accept` command allows you to accept a pending war or scrim you have received. Once accepted, the war or scrim will start automatically. Administrators can accept wars on behalf of other users by mentioning the challenger.
help_accept_usage:
```
$accept
$accept @user
```
• **No arguments**: If you have only one pending war/scrim, execute `$accept`.
• **With @mention**: If you have multiple pending challenges, you must specify from whom: `$accept @user`
• **Administrators**: Administrators can accept wars on behalf of other users using `$accept @challenger` (where @challenger is the one who challenged).
help_accept_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Single challenge**: If you have one pending war or scrim, execute `$accept`.
• **Multiple challenges**: If you have multiple pending challenges, you must specify from whom: `$accept @user`.
• **Immediate acceptance**: Once accepted, the war or scrim will start automatically.
• **Administrators**: If you are a server administrator, you can accept wars on behalf of other users by mentioning the challenger (the one who challenged). This is useful for accepting wars when the opponent is not available. You can only accept one war at a time per challenger.
help_war_description: The `$war` command allows you to challenge another user to a war. A war is a competition of 12 races where each team uses 6 players from their roster. The winner receives the bet coins (if any) and both players can gain or lose Elo based on the result. The request expires in 30 seconds if not accepted.
help_war_usage:
```
$war @user
$war @user amount
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user you want to challenge.
• **amount** (optional): Amount of coins to bet. If not specified, the war will be without a bet.
help_war_details:
• **Challenge**: Creates a request that the opponent can accept (`$accept`) or reject (`$deny`).
• **Timeout**: Expires in 30 seconds without response.
• **Requirements**: Both players need 6+ players in their roster.
• **Bet**: Optional, specify a coin amount.
• **Mechanics**: 12 races, points by position (15-12-10-8-6-4-3-2-1 for top 9).
• **Rewards**: Winner gets bet coins. Both players gain/lose Elo based on result.
• **Lineup**: Uses your 6 lineup players (or auto-selected).
help_scrim_description: The `$scrim` command allows you to challenge another user to a scrim. A scrim is similar to a war (12 races, 6 players per team), but unlike wars, scrims do NOT affect the Elo of participants. Only bet coins are transferred (if any). The request expires in 30 seconds if not accepted.
help_scrim_usage:
```
$scrim @user
$scrim @user amount
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user you want to challenge.
• **amount** (optional): Amount of coins to bet. If not specified, the scrim will be without a bet.
help_scrim_details:
• **Challenge**: Creates a request that the opponent can accept (`$accept`) or reject (`$deny`).
• **Timeout**: Expires in 30 seconds without response.
• **Requirements**: Both players need 6+ players in their roster.
• **Bet**: Optional, specify a coin amount.
• **Mechanics**: 12 races, points by position (15-12-10-8-6-4-3-2-1 for top 9).
• **Rewards**: Winner gets bet coins. Scrims do NOT affect Elo.
• **Lineup**: Uses your 6 lineup players (or auto-selected).
help_tournamentwar_short: Challenge a user to a tournamentwar
help_tournamentwar_description: The `$tournamentwar` (or `$tw`) command allows you to challenge another user to a tournamentwar. A tournamentwar is similar to a war (12 races, 6 players per team), but with important differences: NO coins can be bet, it does NOT affect participants' Elo, and if there is a tie after 12 races, 4 additional tiebreaker races are played. If there is still a tie, 4 more races are played, and so on until there is a winner. The request expires in 30 seconds if not accepted.
help_tournamentwar_usage:
```
$tournamentwar @user
$tw @user
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user you want to challenge.
• **No bets**: Tournamentwars never allow betting coins.
help_tournamentwar_details:
• **Challenge**: Creates a request that the opponent can accept (`$accept`) or reject (`$deny`).
• **Timeout**: Expires in 30 seconds without response.
• **Requirements**: Both players need 6+ players in their roster.
• **No bets**: Tournamentwars do NOT allow betting coins.
• **No Elo**: Tournamentwars do NOT affect participants' Elo.
• **Mechanics**: 12 initial races, points by position (15-12-10-8-6-4-3-2-1 for top 9).
• **Tiebreaker**: If there is a tie after race 12, 4 additional races are played. If there is still a tie, 4 more races are played, and so on until there is a winner.
• **Lineup**: Uses your 6 lineup players (or auto-selected).
help_cpuwar_short: Challenge a CPU team to a war
help_cpuwar_description: The `$cpuwar` (or `$cw`) command allows you to challenge a CPU team to a war. A CPU War is similar to a normal war (12 races, 6 players per team), but you play against an automatically generated CPU team. The CPU team has an average MMR equal to what you specify. NO coins can be bet, but it DOES affect your Elo. The war executes immediately without requiring acceptance.
help_cpuwar_usage:
```
$cpuwar mmr
$cw mmr
```
• **mmr**: MMR of the CPU team (minimum 3000). The CPU team will have 6 players with this MMR.
• **No bets**: CPU Wars never allow betting coins.
• **Immediate execution**: The war starts automatically, no acceptance required.
help_cpuwar_details:
• **Immediate execution**: The war starts automatically, no acceptance or waiting required.
• **Requirements**: You need 6+ players in your roster.
• **Minimum MMR**: The CPU team MMR must be at least 3000.
• **No bets**: CPU Wars do NOT allow betting coins.
• **Affects Elo**: CPU Wars DO affect your Elo (you can gain or lose based on the result).
• **Mechanics**: 12 races, points by position (15-12-10-8-6-4-3-2-1 for top 9).
• **CPU Team**: The CPU team has 6 players with the specified MMR, with no additional attributes.
• **Lineup**: Uses your 6 lineup players (or auto-selected).
• **Energy**: Your team's players lose energy (20-30 points) after the war.
help_thanos_description: The `$thanos` command allows the server owner to execute the "Thanos snap" on the server. This command removes half of all players, reduces Elo and coins to half, and resets all server players' stats. This action is IRREVERSIBLE.
help_thanos_usage:
```
$thanos
```
• **No arguments**: The command does not require arguments. Just execute `$thanos` and confirm with `y` or `n`.
help_thanos_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Server owner only**: This command can only be used by the server owner.
• **Confirmation required**: The command will show a warning and ask for confirmation (y/n) with a 30-second timeout.
• **Irreversible action**: Once confirmed, it executes the "Thanos snap" which:
  - Removes half of each user's players (random, rounding up)
  - Reduces Elo and coins to half for all users
  - Resets all server players' stats (removes all trainings)
• **Statistics**: After execution, it shows statistics of what was removed and affected.

summary_basics_content:
## 📚 Getting Started

Every hour you can perform several rolls with **`$roll`**. In each one you will get a player from Mario Kart World lounge.

Once every 3 hours, by clicking the 'Claim' button on one of those players you can add them to your roster, which you can check by typing **`$roster`**. To see if you have the button available or how much time is left until it recharges, as well as other data about timers, type **`$timerinfo`**.

You can train your players with **`$train`** to make them stronger, then consult what your player's final stats will be with **`$playerstats`**, and face other people with **`$war`** or **`$scrim`**.

Also, twice a day, you can play against the CPU at the level you choose, to test combinations or simply to rank up.

*Ranking up grants you privileges like more rolls per hour or a larger maximum roster size.* You rank up by selling players with $sell and using the coins to buy elo with **`$buyelo`** (though it gets more expensive at each rank), or by winning wars against other people or against the CPU. By ranking up elo, you unlock new ranks that grant you advantages. You can check all information in **`$rankinfo`**.
summary_war_content:
## ⚔️ War System

A war consists of **12 races**, with **6 players per team**.

### The 8 Attributes

Each player has 8 attributes:
- **Lines**: is the pure speed of the player, which will make them gain positions on track and try to place among the top finishers.
- **Consistency**: is the ability to never fail when needed and not fall in complicated strats.
- **Item usage**: ability to get good items to build a good race situation.
- **Precision**: ability to kill other players with aiming items.
- **Communication**: team play, good information in group call, avoid killing teammates unintentionally.
- **Mental**: resistance to breaking down when something goes wrong.
- **Game sense**: ability to predict opponents or dodge their attacks.
- **Shock finding**: ability to get shocks from back items.

### The 4 War Types

There are four types of war available:
- **War** (`$war`): affects both participants' Elo, tires players, may include coin bets and can end in a tie.
- **Scrim** (`$scrim`): does not affect Elo nor tire players, but coins can be bet and it can also end in a tie.
- **Tournament** (`$tournamentwar`): does not affect Elo nor coins, but tires players and never ends in a tie *(in case of a tie, extra races are played)*.
- **CPU War** (`$cpuwar`): is a war against the CPU, at the chosen level, that affects Elo and allows practice.

### War simulation

When starting a war, the bot will follow this process:
- It will create a thread where the lineups, the average attributes of both teams and the initial tracks will be presented.
- Every few seconds it will generate a new message representing a race lap, specifying the actions that each fictional player has been able to carry out (sometimes things happen that are not written in the message so it doesn't get too long, so it may happen that the result has some small discrepancy with the text).
- In each race, teams vote for a track, which may have been configured by the user depending on the situation. Each circuit can be technical, shortcuts, etc., and depending on the type of circuit, some attributes will be more relevant (for example, in shortcut circuits item usage will be more important)
- At the end of each race, the overall standings will be presented, which team is winning and by what difference.
- At the end of the last race, the war will have ended, and the elo change and coin bets will be calculated, if applicable.
summary_advanced_content:
## 🔧 Advanced Commands

### Team Configuration

Use **`$lineup`** to configure the 6 players that will play your next war.

Use **`$trackpick`** with all its options to configure your best tracks in each situation. Use **`$trackinfo`** to see all available tracks and how to write them.

Use **`$teamname`** and **`$tag`** to distinguish yourself from other users and easily identify yourself in your wars.

### Wishlist

Use the **`$wishlist`** to slightly increase the probability of the players you most desire.

### Odds

Check the **`$loungeodds`** to see how many players are in each rank in the current database and what probability you have of getting a player from your wishlist.

### Leaderboards

You can check the elo of all server participants with **`$leaderboard`**, and you can also check a list of the average MMR of the best 6 players of all participants with **`$leaderboardmmr`** (for this particular calculation only the MMR of the 6 best is taken into account, not the user's lineup nor training nor energy)

### ⚠️ Administration

*Be careful with administrators*, who can use **`$coinsremove`**, **`$playerremove`** or even **`$ban`** to control those who don't respect the rules.

Also, from time to time the owner can reset everyone's progress with **`$thanos`**, or directly start the server from scratch with **`$fullreset`**.

help_calc_short: Calculate Elo changes for wars or view your average stats
help_calc_description: The `$calc` command allows you to calculate the Elo changes that would occur in different scenarios of a war (challenger victory, opponent victory, or tie). You can use it in various ways depending on the context: within an active war thread, by mentioning a user to simulate the calculation, or without arguments to see your average stats.
help_calc_usage:
```
$calc
$calc @user
```

**Usage scenarios:**
• **`$calc` with no arguments (outside a thread)**: Shows your average stats based on your current lineup of 6 players.
• **`$calc` with no arguments (inside a normal war thread)**: Calculates Elo changes for the two participants of the active war in that thread. Automatically detects who is the challenger and who is the opponent.
• **`$calc` with no arguments (inside a war vs CPU thread)**: Calculates Elo changes for the person who started the war against the CPU. The command automatically detects who created the thread, so you can use it multiple times without issues.
• **`$calc @user` (outside a thread)**: Simulates the Elo calculation by mentioning a user. You will be the challenger and the mentioned user will be the opponent. Useful to see what would happen if you challenged someone.
• **`$calc` in a scrim thread**: Shows an error message indicating that Elo cannot be calculated in scrims, as scrims do not affect Elo.
help_calc_examples:
**Example 1 - View your average stats:**
```
$calc
```
*Result: Shows your average stats based on your current lineup.*

**Example 2 - Calculate Elo in an active war:**
*You are inside a war thread between @PlayerA and @PlayerB*
```
$calc
```
*Result: Shows Elo changes for both players in the 3 scenarios (A wins, B wins, tie).*

**Example 3 - Calculate Elo in a war vs CPU:**
*You are inside the "war-vs-cpu" thread created by @PlayerX*
```
$calc
```
*Result: Shows Elo changes for @PlayerX against the CPU in the 3 scenarios.*

**Example 4 - Simulate a war:**
*You are in a normal channel, not in a thread*
```
$calc @PlayerY
```
*Result: Simulates Elo changes if you challenged @PlayerY.*
help_calc_details:
**What information does the command show?**

When calculating Elo (not when just viewing your average stats), the command shows:

• **Current status**: The current Elo and rank of both participants (or the player and the CPU).
• **Scenario 1 - Challenger victory**: What would happen to the Elo and rank of both if the challenger wins.
• **Scenario 2 - Opponent victory**: What would happen to the Elo and rank of both if the opponent wins.
• **Scenario 3 - Tie**: What would happen to the Elo and rank of both if there is a tie.

**Important notes:**
• In wars vs CPU, the command always calculates for the person who started the war, not for whoever runs the command.
• You can use `$calc` multiple times in the same thread without issues.
• Scrims do not affect Elo, which is why the command shows an error if you try to use it in a scrim thread.
• To view your average stats, use `$calc` with no arguments outside of any thread.

help_rosterstats_details:
The command displays each player with:
• **Index**: Position number in the roster
• **Name**: Player name (or alias if they have a custom one)
• **Average Stats**: Average of all player statistics (Lines, Consistency, ItemUsage, Precision, Communication, Mental, GameSense, Shockfinding) considering training and energy

Players are automatically sorted by their average stats from highest to lowest, showing the total number of players in the roster.
help_command_not_found_description: No detailed information found for command **{command}**. Use `/help` to see the list of available commands.
help_buyelo_description: The `$buyelo` (or `$be`) command allows you to convert coins into Elo. The Elo cost depends on your current rank (you can check it with `$rankinfo` or `$ri`).
help_buyelo_usage:
```
$buyelo [amount]
$be [amount]
```
• **amount** (optional): Number of coins you want to convert into Elo. If you don't specify an amount, all your available coins will be used (up to the next rank if applicable).
help_buyelo_details:
The command works as follows:
• **No amount**: If you don't specify an amount, all your available coins will be used. If with all your coins you would exceed the next rank, it will automatically limit to the coins needed to reach the next rank.
• **Elo Cost**: The cost depends on your current rank. Each rank has a different cost (see `$rankinfo`).
• **Confirmation**: It will always ask for confirmation (y/n) before making the purchase. You have 30 seconds to respond.
• **Automatic Adjustment**: If the amount of Elo you would buy exceeds the next rank, the bot will automatically adjust the coin amount needed to reach exactly the next rank.
• **Result**: After the purchase, you will see:
- Elo gained
- Coins spent
- New coin balance
- New total Elo
- New rank (if you ranked up)
- Elo to next rank (if there is a next rank and you haven't reached it yet)
help_roll_description: The `$roll` (or `$r`) command allows you to get a random player from the database. Each use consumes one roll from your hourly counter.
help_roll_usage:
```
$roll
$r
```
• **No arguments**: Gets a random player from the database.
help_roll_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Hourly rolls**: You have a limited number of rolls that reset every hour and depend on your rank. The command shows how many rolls you have left.
• **Random player**: You get a random player from the database with all their information:
  - Name
  - Current MMR
  - Peak MMR (maximum reached)
  - Market value
  - Events played
  - Attributes
• **Claim player**: If the player has no owner, a "Claim" button (✅) will appear to claim them and add them to your roster. You can only claim one player every 3 hours.
• **Owned player**: If the player already has an owner, it will show who owns them. In this case, a "Claim" button (💰) will appear that allows you to obtain a percentage of the player's market value as coins based on your rank (as if you were selling them). This also consumes your opportunity to claim a player (CanClaim).
• **Roll consumption**: Each use of the command consumes one roll, even if you don't claim the player.
help_buy_description: The `$buy` command allows you to buy a player that another user has put up for sale using `$sell`. The price is the one the seller specified (or market value if no price was specified).
help_buy_usage:
```
$buy @seller
```
• **@seller**: Mention of the user who has put the player up for sale.
help_buy_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Sale offer**: First, another user must create a sale offer using `$sell @your_user player` or `$sell @your_user player <price>`. This creates a pending offer.
• **Complete purchase**: Use `$buy @seller` to complete the purchase of the player the seller offered.
• **Price**: The price is the one the seller specified (or market value if no price was specified).
• **Payment**: The price is deducted from your coins. The seller receives the agreed price.
• **Transfer**: Once the purchase is completed, the player is automatically transferred to your roster.
help_sell_description: The `$sell` (or `$sl`) command allows you to sell a player from your roster. You can sell it to a specific user (with optional custom price) or to the general market.
help_sell_usage:
```
$sell player
$sl player
$sell @buyer player
$sl @buyer player
$sell @buyer player <price>
$sl @buyer player <price>
```
• **No mention**: Sells the player to the market for a percentage of their market value that depends on your rank (you can check it with `$rankinfo`).
• **With mention, no price**: Creates a sale offer to the mentioned user for the player's market value.
• **With mention and price**: Creates a sale offer to the mentioned user for the specified price (minimum: half of market value rounded down, maximum: double of market value).
help_sell_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Market sale**: No mention (`$sell player`), sell to market for a percentage of market value that depends on your rank (you can check it with `$rankinfo`). Requires confirmation (y/n).
• **Sale to user**: With mention (`$sell @buyer player` or `$sell @buyer player <price>`), create an offer. You can set a custom price (minimum: half of market value, maximum: double). If no price, market value is used.
• **Offer**: Expires after 30 seconds if not completed with `$buy`.
• **Payment**: Market = percentage of value based on your rank. User = specified price (or market value if not specified).
help_trade_description: The `$trade` (or `$tr`) command allows you to exchange a player from your roster for a player from another user's roster. The exchange is direct, with no coin cost.
help_trade_usage:
```
$trade @user myPlayer theirPlayer
$tr @user myPlayer theirPlayer
$trade @user "myPlayer" "theirPlayer"
$tr @user "myPlayer" "theirPlayer"
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user you want to trade with.
• **myPlayer**: Name of the player you want to trade (from your roster).
• **theirPlayer**: Name of the player you want to receive (from the other user's roster).
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the names have multiple words.
help_trade_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Create offer**: When using the command, a trade offer is created that the other user must accept.
• **Confirmation**: The mentioned user will receive a message asking for confirmation (y/n). They have 30 seconds to respond.
• **Direct exchange**: If they accept, the players are automatically exchanged. There is no coin cost, it's a direct exchange.
• **Expiration**: If the other user doesn't respond within 30 seconds, the offer is automatically cancelled.
• **Restrictions**: You cannot trade with yourself. Both users must own their respective players. You cannot exchange the same player.
help_gift_description: The `$gift` (or `$g`) command allows you to gift a player from your roster to another user. The player is transferred directly with no coin cost.
help_gift_usage:
```
$gift player @user
$g player @user
$gift "player name" @user
$g "player name" @user
```
• **player**: Name of the player you want to gift. Must be in your roster.
• **@user**: Mention of the user you want to gift the player to.
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the player name has multiple words.
help_gift_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Gift player**: Transfers the specified player from your roster to the mentioned user.
• **Confirmation**: It will always ask for confirmation (y/n) before making the gift. You have 30 seconds to respond.
• **No cost**: The gift is completely free, there is no coin cost.
• **Transfer**: Once confirmed, the player is automatically transferred to the recipient's roster and removed from your lineup if present.
help_timerinfo_description: The `$timerinfo` (or `$ti`) command shows you information about the bot's timers and resets, including when MMR updates, when you can claim players, and when your rolls reset.
help_timerinfo_details:
The command displays the following information:
• **MMR Update**: Shows how much time is left until the next MMR update (every day at midnight UTC) and the date/time of the next update.
• **Claim**: Shows if you can claim a player (available or unavailable) and how much time is left until the next reset. Claims reset every 3 hours at specific times (00:00, 03:00, 06:00, 09:00, 12:00, 15:00, 18:00, 21:00 UTC).
• **Rolls**: Shows how many rolls you have available and how much time is left until the next reset. Rolls reset every hour at minute 0 (e.g., 14:00, 15:00, 16:00 UTC).
help_trackinfo_description: The `$trackinfo` (or `$tri`) command shows you a list of all available tracks in the bot with their names in all languages (English, Spanish, and French).
help_trackinfo_usage:
```
$trackinfo
$tri
```
• **No arguments**: Shows the complete list of available tracks.
help_trackinfo_details:
The command displays the following information:
• **Track list**: Shows all available tracks numbered, with their abbreviations in brackets and their names in English (🇬🇧), Spanish (🇪🇸), and French (🇫🇷).
• **Usage**: This information is useful for knowing the exact names of tracks when using commands like `$trackpick` or `$trackremove`.
• **Abbreviations**: Abbreviations can be used without quotes in commands (e.g., `$trackpick top MBC`).
help_playerinfo_description: The `$playerinfo` (or `$pi`) command shows you detailed information about a player, including their statistics, attributes, and whether they have an owner in the server.
help_playerinfo_usage:
```
$playerinfo playerName
$pi playerName
```
• **playerName**: Name of the player you want to see information about. Must be the exact player name.
help_playerinfo_details:
The command displays the following information:
• **Basic statistics**: Current MMR, Peak MMR (historical maximum), events played, and market value of the player.
• **Attributes**: Shows the player's 8 attributes (Lines, Consistency, Item Usage, Precision, Communication, Mental, Game Sense, Shockfinding).
• **Owner**: If the player belongs to a user in the server, shows who the owner is. If they don't have an owner, indicates that they don't belong to any user.
• **Embed color**: The embed color changes according to the player's MMR, making it easier to visually identify the rank.
help_wishlist_description: The `$wishlist` (or `$wl`) command allows you to view your wishlist of players or another user's wishlist. The wishlist is a personal list of players you're interested in and increases your chances of getting them when using `$roll` (or `$r`).
help_wishlist_usage:
```
$wishlist
$wl
$wishlist @user
$wl @user
```
• **No arguments**: Shows your own wishlist.
• **@user**: Optional mention of the user whose wishlist you want to see.
help_wishlist_details:
The command displays the following information:
• **Player list**: Shows all players in the wishlist with their name, MMR, Peak MMR, and events played.
• **Wishlist limit**: The maximum number of players you can have in your wishlist depends on your rank. You can see your current limit in the message.
• **Function**: Players in your wishlist have a higher probability of appearing when you use the `$roll` (or `$r`) command.
• **Related commands**: Use `$wishlistadd playerName` (or `$wla playerName`) to add players and `$wishlistremove playerName` (or `$wlr playerName`) to remove them from your wishlist.
help_stop_description: The `$stop` command allows you to request stopping an active war. It requires both participants to request stopping it for it to actually stop.
help_stop_usage:
```
$stop
```
• **No arguments**: Requests to stop the active war in the current thread.
help_stop_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Thread usage**: Can only be used within the thread of an active war. It doesn't work in normal channels.
• **Participants**: Only the war participants (the challenger and the opponent) can request to stop it.
• **Mutual confirmation**: Both participants must use `$stop` for the war to stop. If only one requests it, it will wait for the other to do so as well.
• **Stopping**: Once both participants have requested to stop the war, it will stop at the next race and the final points will be shown.
help_deny_description: The `$deny` command allows you to reject a pending war or scrim. When someone challenges you with `$war` or `$scrim`, you can use this command to reject the challenge.
help_deny_usage:
```
$deny
$deny @user
```
• **No arguments**: If you have only one pending war/scrim, execute `$deny`.
• **With @mention**: If you have multiple pending challenges, you must specify from whom: `$deny @user`
help_deny_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Single challenge**: If you have one pending war or scrim, execute `$deny`.
• **Multiple challenges**: If you have multiple pending challenges, you must specify from whom: `$deny @user`.
• **Opponent only**: Only the user who was mentioned as the opponent can reject.
• **No cost**: Rejecting a challenge has no cost or consequences.
• **Alternative**: You can also use `$accept` if you want to accept the challenge instead.
help_teamname_description: The `$teamname` (or `$tn`) command allows you to change your team name. The team name will be displayed in wars, scrims, and other places where your team is identified.
help_teamname_usage:
```
$teamname New Team Name
$tn New Team Name
```
• **New Team Name**: The new name you want to assign to your team. Can contain spaces.
help_teamname_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Name change**: Changes your team name to the specified name.
• **Usage**: The team name will be displayed in wars, scrims, and in your user information (`$userinfo`).
help_editteamname_description: The `$editteamname` (or `$etn`) command allows an administrator to change another user's team name. This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
help_editteamname_usage:
```
$editteamname @user New Team Name
$etn @user New Team Name
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user whose team name you want to change.
• **New Team Name**: The new name you want to assign to the user's team. Can contain spaces.
help_editteamname_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Permissions**: Only administrators can use this command.
• **Name change**: Changes the mentioned user's team name to the specified name.
• **Validations**: The name cannot be empty, must meet the maximum character limit, and cannot be the same name the user already has.
help_userinfo_description: The `$userinfo` (or `$ui`) command shows you detailed information about a user, including their team, tag, coins, Elo, rank, selected tracks, and lineup.
help_userinfo_usage:
```
$userinfo
$ui
$userinfo @user
$ui @user
```
• **No arguments**: Shows your own information.
• **@user**: Optional mention of the user whose information you want to see.
help_userinfo_details:
The command displays the following information:
• **Team and Tag**: Shows the user's team name and tag.
• **Coins and Elo**: Shows the amount of coins and Elo the user has.
• **Rank**: Shows the user's current rank with its corresponding emoji.
• **Tracks**: Shows the tracks selected by the user for each type (balanced, top, antitop, bottom).
• **Lineup**: Shows the user's current lineup (up to 6 players). If there are empty slots, it's indicated with `+N` where N is the number of missing slots.
help_tag_description: The `$tag` command allows you to change your tag. The tag is an abbreviation that is displayed alongside your team name in wars and other places.
help_tag_usage:
```
$tag NewTag
```
• **NewTag**: The new tag you want to assign. Can contain special characters and has a maximum limit of 5 characters.
help_tag_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Tag change**: Changes your tag to the specified tag.
• **Usage**: The tag will be displayed in wars, scrims, and in your user information (`$userinfo`). If two users have the same tag in a war, a number will be added at the end to differentiate them (e.g., "SER1" and "SER2").
help_alias_description: The `$alias` (or `$a`) command allows you to change the alias (custom name) of a player in your roster. The alias will be displayed instead of the player's original name in your roster and other places.
help_alias_usage:
```
$alias playerName newAlias
$a playerName newAlias
$alias playerName "new alias"
$a playerName "new alias"
```
• **playerName**: Name of the player in your roster whose alias you want to change.
• **newAlias**: The new alias you want to assign to the player.
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the alias has multiple words.
help_alias_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Alias change**: Changes the alias of the specified player to the new alias. The player must be in your roster.
• **Alias usage**: The alias will be displayed in your roster (`$roster`) and in wars or scrims.
help_lineup_description: The `$lineup` (or `$lu`) command allows you to set your complete lineup at once. It completely replaces your previous lineup with the players you specify.
help_lineup_usage:
```
$lineup "Player1" "Player2" "Player3"
$lu "Player1" "Player2"
$lineup "Player1"
```
• **Players in quotes**: Each player must be in double quotes. You can specify from 1 to 6 players.
• **Complete replacement**: This command completely replaces your previous lineup. If you specify fewer than 6 players, the remaining slots will be empty.
• **Players in your roster**: All players must be in your roster.
help_lineup_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Set complete lineup**: Completely replaces your previous lineup with the players you specify.
• **Quotes required**: Each player must be in double quotes. Example: `$lineup "Player1" "Player2"`
• **Maximum 6 players**: You can specify up to 6 players. If you specify fewer, the remaining slots will be empty.
• **Players in your roster**: All players must be in your roster. If any player is not in your roster, you'll receive an error indicating which ones were not found.
help_lineupadd_description: The `$lineupadd` (or `$lua`) command allows you to add players to your lineup. The lineup is your team of up to 6 players that you'll use in wars and scrims.
help_lineupadd_usage:
```
$lineupadd player
$lua player
$lineupadd player1, player2, player3
$lua player1, player2, player3
```
• **player**: Name of the player you want to add to your lineup. Must be in your roster.
• **Multiple players**: To add multiple players at once, separate them with commas. You can add up to 6 players in total.
help_lineupadd_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Add players**: Adds the specified players to your lineup. Players must be in your roster.
• **Lineup limit**: The lineup can have a maximum of 6 players. If you try to add more than can fit, you'll receive an error indicating how many slots are available.
• **Comma separation**: To add multiple players, separate them with commas. If you don't use commas, all text will be treated as a single player.
• **Already present players**: If you try to add a player that's already in your lineup, you'll receive an error.
help_lineupremove_description: The `$lineupremove` (or `$lur`) command allows you to remove players from your lineup. Removed players will remain in your roster, they'll only be removed from your lineup.
help_lineupremove_usage:
```
$lineupremove player
$lur player
$lineupremove player1, player2, player3
$lur player1, player2, player3
```
• **player**: Name of the player you want to remove from your lineup.
• **Multiple players**: To remove multiple players at once, separate them with commas.
help_lineupremove_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Remove players**: Removes the specified players from your lineup. Players must currently be in your lineup.
• **Comma separation**: To remove multiple players, separate them with commas. If you don't use commas, all text will be treated as a single player.
• **Players not found**: If you try to remove a player that's not in your lineup, you'll receive an error indicating which players weren't found.
• **Empty lineup**: If your lineup is already empty, you'll receive an error.
help_removealias_description: The `$removealias` (or `$ra`) command allows you to remove the alias of one of your own players. This command can be used by any user.
help_removealias_usage:
```
$removealias player
$ra player
$removealias "player name"
$ra "player name"
```
• **player**: Name of the player whose alias you want to remove. Must be in your roster.
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the player name has multiple words.
help_removealias_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Your players only**: You can only remove the alias of players that are in your own roster.
• **No mentions**: This command does not allow mentioning other users. It only works for yourself.
• **Remove alias**: Removes the alias of the specified player. The player will return to showing their original name.
• **Player without alias**: If the player doesn't have an alias, you'll receive an error indicating that player doesn't have an alias.
help_removealiasuser_description: The `$removealiasuser` (or `$rau`) command allows you to remove the alias of a player from another user. This command can only be used by server administrators.
help_removealiasuser_usage:
```
$removealiasuser @user player
$rau @user player
$removealiasuser @user "player name"
$rau @user "player name"
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user from whom you want to remove the player's alias.
• **player**: Name of the player whose alias you want to remove. Must be in the mentioned user's roster.
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the player name has multiple words.
help_removealiasuser_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Administrators only**: Only users with administrator permissions on the server can use this command.
• **Remove alias**: Removes the alias of the specified player from the mentioned user. The player will return to showing their original name.
• **Player without alias**: If the player doesn't have an alias, you'll receive an error indicating that player doesn't have an alias.
help_removeplayer_description: The `$removeplayer` (or `$rp`) command allows an administrator to remove a player from another user's roster and return them to the market. This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
help_removeplayer_usage:
```
$removeplayer @user player
$rp @user player
$removeplayer @user "player name"
$rp @user "player name"
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user from whom you want to remove the player.
• **player**: Name or alias of the player you want to remove. Must be in the mentioned user's roster.
• **Quotes**: Optional, but recommended if the player name has multiple words.
help_removeplayer_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Permissions**: Only administrators can use this command.
• **Remove player**: Removes the specified player from the mentioned user's roster and returns them to the market, where they'll be available for other users to obtain.
• **Alias**: You can use the player's original name or the alias the user has assigned to them.
• **Lineup**: If the player was in the user's lineup, they'll also be automatically removed from the lineup.
help_clearroster_description: The `$clearroster` command allows an administrator to delete all players from a user's roster. All players will be removed from the Ownership and Player tables. This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
help_clearroster_usage:
```
$clearroster @user
$clearroster TeamName
```
• **@user**: Mention of the user whose roster you want to clear.
• **TeamName**: Team name of the user whose roster you want to clear.
help_clearroster_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Permissions**: Only administrators can use this command.
• **Delete all players**: Deletes all players from the specified user's roster.
• **Complete deletion**: Players are deleted from the Ownership and Player tables, and are also removed from the lineup if they were in it.
• **Search by mention or teamname**: You can specify the user by mentioning them or by typing their team name.

clearroster_no_permission: ❌ You don't have permission to use this command. Only administrators can use `$clearroster`.
clearroster_no_mention_or_teamname: ❌ You must mention a user or specify the team name. Use: `$clearroster @user` or `$clearroster TeamName`

help_rankinfo_description: The `$rankinfo` (or `$ri`) command shows you detailed information about all available ranks in the bot, including their benefits and features. It also shows your current rank or the mentioned user's rank.
help_rankinfo_usage:
```
$rankinfo
$ri
$rankinfo @user
$ri @user
```
• **No arguments**: Shows information about all ranks and your current rank.
• **@user**: Optional mention of the user whose rank you want to see.
help_rankinfo_details:
The command displays the following information for each rank:
• **Rolls per hour**: Number of rolls available each hour based on rank.
• **Training sessions**: Number of training sessions available based on rank.
• **Wishlists**: Maximum number of players you can have in your wishlist.
• **Wishlist mult.**: Probability multiplier for players in your wishlist.
• **Max roster**: Maximum number of players you can have in your roster.
• **Elo cost**: Cost in coins per Elo point when buying Elo.
• **Elo needed**: Amount of Elo required to reach that rank.
• **Default sell benefit**: Percentage of market value you receive when selling a player to the market. For example, in the wood rank you will receive 50% of the value, while in the god rank you will receive 100% of the value.

The arrows (▶️◀️) indicate the current rank of the queried user (you or the mentioned user). Ranks update automatically based on your Elo.

help_allowsteal_description: The `$allowsteal` (or `$as`) command allows an administrator to configure whether any user can claim players rolled by other users or only the roller. This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
help_allowsteal_usage:
```
$allowsteal
$as
$allowsteal 0
$as 0
$allowsteal 1
$as 1
```
• **No arguments**: Shows the current configuration status.
• **0**: Only the user who rolled can claim the player (default behavior).
• **1**: Any user can claim players rolled by others.
help_allowsteal_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Administrators only**: This command can only be used by users with administrator permissions.
• **Default behavior (0)**: By default, only the user who rolled ($roll or $r) can claim the player they got. This prevents other users from "stealing" players.
• **Allow steal (1)**: If set to 1, any user can click the claim button on players rolled by other users, allowing for a more competitive game mode.
• **Check status**: If you don't provide any arguments, the command will show the current server configuration.
• **Immediate change**: The change is applied immediately and affects all future rolls on the server.
help_playerstats_description: The `$playerstats` (or `$ps`) command shows detailed statistics of a player, including their attributes with MMR added and a development progress bar.
help_playerstats_usage:
```
$playerstats playerName
$ps playerName
```
• **playerName**: Name of the player whose statistics you want to see.
help_playerstats_details:
The command works as follows:
• **Attributes**: Shows the player's 8 attributes (Lines, Consistency, Item usage, Precision, Communication, Mental, Game sense, Shockfinding). Each attribute adds its base value plus the player's MMR (minimum 0).
• **Progress bar**: Indicates the player's development level. 0% = 330 points or less, 100% = 8000 points or more. Values in between are calculated linearly.
• **Format**: Displayed as 'Attribute: Value with MMR', clearly showing the effective value of each statistic.
